rationale: A wrong RK4 stage weight (k2 used twice, k3 dropped) still sums to one and still holds a trim, but it drops the method to second order; the order test must see a ratio of 4 instead of 16.

pattern: uStage = u0 + [inputAt(tk, tk), inputAt(tk + dt/2, tk), inputAt(tk + dt, tk)];
rationale: Sampling a smooth input once at the step start instead of at the RK4 stage times silently turns the simulation into a first-order method whenever an input is applied.

replacement: uStage = [ctrl.step(tk, x, struct(), u0 + inputAt(tk, tk), cstate), ctrl.step(tk + dt/2, x, struct(), u0 + inputAt(tk + dt/2, tk), cstate), ctrl.step(tk + dt, x, struct(), u0 + inputAt(tk + dt, tk), cstate)];
rationale: A discrete controller re-evaluated at every RK4 stage instead of zero-order held misrepresents the sampled system (CONVENTIONS 10); its closed-loop behaviour and order would be wrong.
A disabled ground guard lets a run continue below the terrain and report it as completed.
A stop time recorded one step late misplaces the event (e.g. ground contact, loss of attitude integrity) against the logged state.
